concept.name: Horizontal channel
concept.definition: A channel whose two parallel boundary lines are roughly horizontal, enclosing a sideways market: resistance above and support below at approximately constant prices. It represents consolidation or indecision and is the channel equivalent of a trading range.
concept.intuition: Price bounces between a flat floor and a flat ceiling while the market makes up its mind.
concept.mechanics: Constructed by drawing a horizontal line across the reaction highs and a parallel horizontal line across the reaction lows. Range-trading heuristics buy support and sell resistance until a decisive breakout occurs; the direction of the eventual break is treated as the resolution signal.
concept.failure_modes: Horizontal channels produce repeated false breaks at both rails; tight stops just outside the rails are exactly where whipsaws cluster.
concept.misconceptions: That a horizontal channel's eventual break is equally likely up or down in all contexts; prior trend and volume behavior skew the odds, though never to certainty.
concept.example: A stock oscillates between 70 support and 75 resistance for weeks, forming a horizontal channel, until a high-volume close above 75 resolves it upward.
